start_date.notes: Day-of-month and month are both directly stated for every one of the 8 performer entries (e.g. VANESSA FERREIRA: days 1 and 29, 'de Agosto'), mechanically confirmed in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt. But NO 4-digit year appears anywhere in the retained performer/day summary block, the item's own description/content/schedule_text/schedule_header fields, or anywhere else in the retained HTML or JSON for this candidate -- mechanically confirmed by a direct regex scan finding zero year tokens. The JSON's own date_begin/date_end fields ('2025-10-24'..'2027-12-31') do NOT resolve this: they span more than one distinct calendar year, so more than one real August (2026 and 2027) falls inside that window -- mechanically confirmed in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt. This is further corroborated by cross-checking a genuinely one-off, specifically-dated show in the same retained JSON ('ABBA MIA', whose own schedule_text states only 'DATA: 11 Outubro' with no year either, and whose own date_begin/date_end is likewise a generic full-calendar-year display-visibility window, not the show's real date) -- proving date_begin/date_end is a content-visibility window this CMS uses site-wide, never the actual occurrence date, and that omitting the year from schedule_text is a systemic site convention, not a gap unique to this candidate. Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's date/time rule and its v1.2 worked-examples table, inferring a specific year (e.g. '2026' merely because that is the current real-world year) would be exactly the prohibited AI_INFERENCE pattern, not a mechanical DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT combination with exactly one valid result -- there are genuinely two structurally-plausible years (2026, 2027) within the record's own retained validity window, so no single result is determinable. Stays AMBIGUOUS rather than PROVEN or PARTIAL: day and month are known, year is not, and this is not a case where the source's own structure settles the ambiguity.

price.notes: The candidate's own retained schedule_text field states directly: 'ENTRADA: LIVRE*' (free entry), matching the page's own sidebar contact box ('ENTRADA: LIVRE*'). The JSON record's separate 'price' field is an empty string (not itself a usable value), so this claim rests on schedule_text, which does state it explicitly and directly -- not combined from separate context, hence DIRECT_SOURCE rather than DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT. HONEST CAVEAT, not smoothed over: the retained page's own footnote states the asterisk means 'Às sextas-feiras, sábados e em noites temáticas, é obrigatório o consumo mínimo para lugares sentados na zona de bar' (on Fridays, Saturdays, and themed nights, a minimum consumption charge is mandatory for seated bar-area seating) -- so 'FREE' is an honest characterisation of admission itself, but not an unconditional zero-cost guarantee for every seating arrangement on every night.

blockers.description: The exact calendar year of every one of the 8 currently-listed performance dates is never stated anywhere in retained evidence: not in the candidate page's own server-rendered HTML, not in the referenced JSON asset's own description/content/schedule_text/schedule_header fields for this candidate, and not mechanically resolvable from the JSON's own date_begin/date_end fields (empirically proven, via offline-proof, to be a generic content-visibility window rather than the real occurrence date -- it spans more than one distinct calendar year, and the same imprecise pattern was independently confirmed on a genuinely one-off, specifically-dated show, 'ABBA MIA', in the same retained JSON). A collector built on this source today could only fill in a year by assuming 'the nearest/current one' from today's real-world date -- exactly the AI_INFERENCE pattern docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md prohibits from ever becoming a PROVEN fact. Until the source itself begins stating the year (directly, or via some other retained, mechanically-combinable first-party context), no automated collector can honestly produce a dated Observation from this candidate.

No source-documented per-night identifier or per-night URL exists (see field_assessment.source_record_id.notes and field_assessment.event_url.notes) -- all 8 currently-listed nights share one series-level slug/URL. Even once the CRITICAL year blocker above is resolved, a collector would still need to synthesize a composite (venue + room + calendar date) key rather than relying on any id from the source itself.

The nightly default start time (22h00) is stated once as a page-level/series-level constant, but the source's own retained content already demonstrates at least one genuine per-night exception (MANUEL MELO, 23h00) -- a collector that hard-codes the constant without checking for a stated per-entry override would misdate that specific night.

The 'FREE' admission claim carries a source-stated asterisked exception (mandatory minimum consumption for seated bar-area seating on Fridays, Saturdays, and themed nights) that a flat 'FREE' price field would silently lose unless a collector also propagates the footnote text.

reasons: This candidate's structural shape (a genuinely server-rendered public page plus a publicly-referenced, structured JSON data asset naming performer, day-of-month, month, room, admission, and default schedule) is otherwise a clean, honest fit for automated acquisition -- title, time, end, venue_location, and price all reach PROVEN with cited, retained, mechanically-reproduced evidence, and none of this required browser/headless observation.

However, field_assessment.start_date honestly reaches only AMBIGUOUS: the retained evidence establishes day-of-month and month for every listed performer, but no 4-digit year is stated anywhere on this source for this candidate, and the JSON's own date_begin/date_end field -- which might otherwise have resolved this -- was empirically proven (via offline-proof, and via a corroborating cross-check against a genuinely one-off, specifically-dated show in the same JSON) to be a generic content-visibility window rather than the real occurrence date, spanning more than one distinct calendar year.

Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's date/time rule and its v1.2 field-value-basis worked examples, promoting a specific year to PROVEN here -- merely because today's real-world date (2026-08-27) makes '2026' the obvious guess -- would be exactly the prohibited AI_INFERENCE pattern, not a genuine DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT combination with exactly one valid result. This investigation deliberately does not do that.

Because the year cannot be honestly established, field_assessment.source_record_id also cannot reach a safe alternative identity strategy: the obvious composite (slug + calendar date) key used successfully in fama-dalfama-lisbon-01 is not viable here without an unresolved/guessed year, which this policy explicitly prohibits inventing.

collector_assessment.blockers records this honestly as a single CRITICAL blocker (plus three MINOR ones) rather than smoothing it into a MINOR note or silently working around it -- READY_FOR_ACTIVATION explicitly requires no unresolved CRITICAL blocker, and this investigation does not attempt to force that gate.

Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's escalation ladder, DEFER never requires exhausting or even attempting every probe level: the blocking finding here is a genuine absence of year data in the source's own server-rendered HTML and its own JSON asset, not a client-rendering or hidden-data-path problem that a Level 2/3/4 probe could plausibly resolve, so this investigation stops at a single, SUFFICIENT Level 1 probe_history entry rather than opening a browser session merely to appear thorough.

This is a legitimate, complete, evidenced investigation outcome, not a failure -- see docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's 'Level 5 -- Defer' section. A future re-investigation (a new investigation_id, superseding this one) may reach a different conclusion if the source itself later begins stating the year, or if some other retained, mechanically-combinable first-party context (e.g. a dated page revision, a differently-structured programme page) is found.
This decision is a research conclusion only -- it does not edit sources/*.json or any registry; it does not change sources/lisbon.json's existing 'casino-estoril-musica-ao-vivo' entry in any way.
